subject: Follow-up: Audit logs & data access (Finco Bank)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@fincobank.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fincobank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Audit logs & data access (Finco Bank)

Hi Sarah / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to get a clearer sense of your compliance bar. Per our conversation, a few quick notes & asks so we can scope the work and pricing: 

- What you said: Finco needs per-request audit logs (who accessed what and when) for any exported content that may contain PII, retained for 7 years, and an exportable format for legal/forensics.
- We need to confirm the set of identities that must be logged (service accounts vs human users) and whether you require redaction/pseudonymization in the exported files.
- Export formats: we can provide CSV, JSONL, or Parquet. CSV is easiest for spreadsheets; JSONL preserves nested metadata (IP, session_id, model_version).
- Retention: Redwood stores audit logs for 1 year by default in hosted; Dedicated/Private deployments can configure retention policies. For Dedicated we can increase retention to 7 yrs with archived cold storage — will outline costs.

Can you confirm:
1) the list of roles (emails) that must be included in logs as internal Finco actors?
2) whether exports need to include full request/response text, or just metadata (user id, timestamp, action, model_id, tokens)?
3) whether Finco requires data residency (US-only) for these logs?

I attached a short evidence checklist we typically use and an audit log template (sample CSV/fields). If you can confirm the answers above by end of day Thursday, we can scope an evidence package and estimated pricing for extended retention.

Next steps from our side: Aditya and Ben will prepare a sample export and a short doc explaining export fields and retention options.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: evidence_request_checklist.pdf, audit_log_template.csv

From: Sarah Lee <sarah.lee@fincobank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@fincobank.com>
Date: 2026-05-30T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Audit logs & data access (Finco Bank)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap and the templates — very helpful. Quick answers inline: 

1) Roles: we need logs for all human users (email addresses in our org) and any service accounts tied to downstream data exports. I can send a canonical list by EOD Friday.
2) Export content: For legal/forensics we need the request and metadata; the full response text is preferred but we understand redaction options may be needed for sensitive PII. Can you outline redaction approaches (hashing, token-level redaction) and how that affects reconstruction for legal requests?
3) Residency: yes, logs must be stored in US-only regions (we are regulated under US banking rules).

Also: sample exports should include a mapping of internal IDs to human-readable emails — we can provide a mapping file if you need it. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

-Sarah
Head of InfoSec | Finco Bank
sarah.lee@fincobank.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Audit logs & data access (Finco Bank)

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the quick reply and the clarifications — that helps a lot. A few follow-ups and what we can deliver this week: 

- Redaction approaches: we support (1) full-text export (raw request/response), (2) token-level redaction where identifiable tokens are replaced with deterministic hashes, and (3) metadata-only export. For legal purposes most customers ask for deterministic hashing + a separate mapping (stored by the customer) so you can correlate without Redwood holding raw PII for long retention durations. We'll include a short appendix on reconstruction tradeoffs.
- Residency: we can keep logs in US-only regions for Dedicated or Private deployments; hosted API customers can choose US-region storage for logs (we will flag cross-region egress when relevant).
- Export formats: we'll generate a sample CSV and a JSONL with the following fields: timestamp, actor_email (or actor_id), action (generate/export/download), model_id, request_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, ip_address, session_id, redaction_status. Attached is a sample_kv_export.jsonl (snippet) and the audit_log_template.csv.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: we’ll send sample exports + mapping of fields (Aditya + Ben).
- Tue 6/2: we can produce a short written evidence package (SOC2-aligned mapping of controls + sample exports).
- By 6/9: scope retention pricing for 7-year cold storage for Dedicated/Private.

Action for you: please send the list of roles/service accounts and confirm whether you want raw text or hashed redaction for the initial evidence package.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachments: sample_kv_export.jsonl, audit_log_template.csv, evidence_request_checklist.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Marissa / Ben —

I pulled the sample from the staging cluster and attached a 1k-line snippet to the drive folder linked below. Plan: produce both CSV and JSONL samples with two variants: raw_text and hashed_pii. Fields included: timestamp, actor_id, actor_email (hashed), action, model_version, request_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, ip, session_id, retention_tag.

Questions for Marissa:
- Which hashed approach should we use for actor_email in the evidence package (sha256 salted with customer-supplied salt, or deterministic reversible mapping)? My recommendation: sha256 salted with customer salt — gives Finco the ability to map if they hold the salt but avoids Redwood storing reversible mappings.
- Do we need to include the full response text in the evidence set or omit for the initial package?

I'll add the files to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-evidence and flag the sample names.
